question: Can the existing moving-window controller after the same 500-global prefix reduce hybrid tail chattering without losing its positive development fairness gain or increasing total cost beyond fixed hybrid?
hypothesis: The fixed window=100, alpha=2 cap will reduce both exact pair-gap crossings and target switches relative to fixed hybrid while retaining lower Gini than Classical and total mean token cost no greater than hybrid.
falsifier: Failure of any one of the four frozen promotion conditions prevents opening a fresh confirmation domain for this candidate.

data.split: TICO development, 970 fixed aligned en/fr/es rows
data.exposure: development; already exposed and allowed for this candidate

arms.candidate: author moving-window PA-BPE, global_merges=500, window_size=100, alpha=2, 1000 merges
comparators: fixed hybrid with 500 global then base controller

quality_metrics: Gini of per-language mean token costs

promotion_conditions.cost: candidate total mean token cost <= hybrid total mean token cost

resource_authorization.memory_basis: prior comparable author run peak <115 MiB; require 512 MiB measured cgroup headroom at launch

interpretation.all_conditions_pass: Candidate may be frozen for a genuinely fresh confirmation domain.
interpretation.otherwise: Retain as a development negative or partial mechanism result; do not inspect a new confirmation domain.
